material_claims.current_R6_wording: forcing buyers onto social DM or a phone call at the exact moment they are comparing homes raises drop-off between 'found a development' and 'booked a viewing', suppressing the viewing reservations that drive Persimmon's sales funnel
material_claims.pdf_section: Executive Summary — Key Decisions · Finding 1 · Implementation Brief ACT-001
material_claims.directly_observed: The Contact Us page contains zero web enquiry forms (0 <form> elements in live HTML read 2026-09-14). Enquiry routes are social media DMs (Facebook Messenger / Instagram DM) and a regional-office drop-down.
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: That forcing buyers onto social DM or phone raises drop-off; that viewing reservations are being suppressed; that a web form would increase reservations.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Drop-off, reservation suppression and funnel impact are inferred from the absence of a form, not measured. A buyer may successfully book viewings via phone/DM — the public page cannot establish conversion impact.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: The Contact Us page currently routes all enquiries through social media DMs (staffed evenings to 9.30pm, weekends 8.30am–9.30pm) and a regional-office drop-down — there is no web enquiry form. The page currently does X (routes through social DM / phone). Public research cannot establish whether this creates friction at the moment a buyer has found a development, or how many enquiries are lost. This may create friction. Validate with CRM enquiry-source data, phone/DM volume, regional-sales feedback and GA4 enquiry-to-viewing progression before scaling.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: The Contact Us page has no visible web enquiry form — enquiries route through social DM and a regional-office drop-down. Not established by public research: whether this currently reduces enquiry volume, viewing bookings, reservation intent or conversion rate. Hypothesis to validate: a central development-aware enquiry form may capture peak-interest intent more reliably. Validate with: CRM enquiry-source data, phone/DM volume, regional-sales feedback, GA4 enquiry-to-viewing progression.
material_claims.validation_data_source: CRM enquiry-source records, phone/DM volume logs, regional-sales feedback, GA4 events (enquiry_start, viewing_booked)
material_claims.claim_type: customer-data-dependent claim (hypothesis: friction exists; outcome requires customer data)
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: Separates the observable fact (no form) from the unproven consequence (lost reservations). The customer can verify the observation themselves and understands that the recommendation's impact needs their own data — this makes the action credible without making it weak.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: first-time buyers may be a particularly research-heavy segment
material_claims.directly_observed: FTB page discusses budgeting steps, scheme names (Deposit Boost, Shared Ownership) and includes a mid-paragraph link to an affordability calculator. No comparison tool or eligibility checker exists.
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: That FTBs are the largest or most research-heavy segment; that requiring human contact for scheme comparison causes decision deferral.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Segment size and research behaviour are internal customer data not observable from public pages.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: The First-time-buyers page describes schemes in prose spread across paragraphs — Deposit Boost, Shared Ownership, Mortgage Assist — with no side-by-side comparison and no eligibility checker. The page currently does X (prose-only scheme description). Public research cannot establish whether first-time buyers are the most research-heavy segment, or how many defer a decision when comparison requires a phone call. This may create friction for research-phase buyers. Validate with CRM enquiry-by-segment data, GA4 audience reports and regional-sales feedback.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: First-time-buyer schemes are described in prose without a comparison tool or eligibility checker. Not established by public research: which buyer segment is largest, or whether research-phase buyers defer when comparison requires human contact. Hypothesis to validate: a self-check tool may reduce deferral for research-phase first-time buyers. Validate with: CRM enquiry-by-segment data, GA4 audience reports, regional-sales feedback.
material_claims.validation_data_source: Persimmon CRM enquiry-by-segment data, GA4 audience/behaviour reports, regional-sales feedback
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: Names the validation data source (CRM + GA4) so the customer knows exactly what evidence would confirm or refute the hypothesis. Avoids vague disclaimers by tying the hypothesis to a measurable outcome.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: the buyer defers the decision and the enquiry is lost to aggregators/portals that do offer instant comparison, suppressing Persimmon's direct-enquiry funnel
material_claims.directly_observed: No scheme comparison tool exists on FTB or Flexible Help pages (live HTML read 2026-09-14).
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: That buyers actually exit to aggregator portals; the volume of direct-enquiry suppression.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Aggregator-leakage is a competitive-dynamics claim that cannot be verified without traffic and CRM data.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: No scheme comparison tool exists on the researched pages. The page currently does X (prose-only scheme description). Public research cannot establish whether buyers exit to aggregator portals or how many enquiries are lost this way. Hypothesis to validate: a comparison tool may retain research-phase buyers who would otherwise defer. Validate with GA4 exit-page and referral data, CRM lost-enquiry reason tracking and competitor monitoring.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: no scheme comparison tool exists on the researched pages. Not established by public research: whether buyers exit to aggregator portals, or the volume of any enquiry loss. Hypothesis to validate: a comparison tool may retain research-phase buyers. Validate with: GA4 exit-page and referral data, CRM lost-enquiry reasons, competitor monitoring.
material_claims.validation_data_source: GA4 exit-page and referral data, CRM lost-enquiry reason tracking, competitor monitoring
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: Replaces a definitive competitive-dynamics claim ('enquiry is lost to aggregators') with a testable hypothesis tied to a specific data source. Keeps the recommendation actionable without claiming market knowledge the report cannot have.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: repeat research traffic gets no re-engagement channel (hypothesis to validate with analytics: this may be the highest-intent segment) and Persimmon has no permission-based way to bring buyers back
material_claims.directly_observed: No save-search or email-alert functionality on /find-your-new-home (live HTML read 2026-09-14). Search filters (location, distance, price) exist but results cannot be saved.
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: The volume of repeat research visits; whether an alert would increase return visits, enquiries or reservations.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Repeat-visit volume and alert effectiveness require analytics data not available from public pages.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: The find-your-new-home page offers location, distance and price filters but no save-search or email-alert feature. The page currently does X (search without re-engagement). Public research cannot establish how many buyers return repeatedly without an alert, or whether an alert would increase enquiries. Hypothesis to validate: a permission-based alert may create a re-engagement channel for repeat search visitors. Validate with GA4 return-visitor rate, post-launch alert sign-up/open/enquiry metrics, CRM follow-up data.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: no save-search or email-alert feature exists on /find-your-new-home. Not established by public research: current repeat-visit volume or whether an alert would increase it. Hypothesis to validate: a permission-based alert may create a re-engagement channel. Validate with: GA4 return-visitor rate, post-launch alert sign-up/open/enquiry metrics, CRM follow-up data.
material_claims.validation_data_source: GA4 return-visitor rate, post-launch alert sign-up/open/enquiry metrics, CRM follow-up data
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: The observation (no alert feature) is verifiable; the impact (re-engagement value) is honestly unproven. The customer understands exactly what data would prove it.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: Movers with an existing home are a high-intent buyer segment (hypothesis to validate with CRM sales data) for part exchange; when combinability is unclear, the customer assumes ineligibility
material_claims.directly_observed: Flexible Help page describes Part Exchange and Deposit Boost separately; combinability is addressed only in T&C clauses 4.4-4.6 (buried at the bottom).
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: That unclear combinability causes buyers to assume ineligibility or reduces enquiries.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Buyer assumption of ineligibility is a behavioural inference not observable from public pages.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: Part Exchange and Deposit Boost are described separately on the Flexible Help page; combinability is addressed only in T&C clauses 4.4-4.6, which state that Part Exchange is excluded when buying with certain schemes. The page currently does X (separate scheme descriptions, combinability in T&Cs). Public research cannot establish whether buyers assume ineligibility when combinability is unclear, or how many enquiries are lost as a result. Hypothesis to validate: a combinability summary may reduce buyer uncertainty. Validate with CRM part-exchange enquiry data, GA4 page-exit rates on /flexiblehelp, regional-sales feedback.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: Part Exchange and Deposit Boost are described separately; combinability is addressed only in T&C clauses 4.4-4.6. Not established by public research: whether unclear combinability causes buyers to assume ineligibility or reduces enquiries. Hypothesis to validate: a combinability summary may reduce buyer uncertainty. Validate with: CRM part-exchange enquiry data, GA4 page-exit rates, regional-sales feedback.
material_claims.validation_data_source: CRM part-exchange enquiry data, GA4 page-exit rates on /flexiblehelp, regional-sales feedback
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: The T&C clauses are quoted verbatim as observation; the behavioural inference is separated as hypothesis. The customer can check clause 4.4 themselves.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: a visible customer-facing timeline converts that abstract advantage into perceived certainty, which is the primary emotional driver lifting a prospect's reservation intent during the research phase
material_claims.directly_observed: 'no buying chains' claim exists on the FTB page; no visual purchase-timeline module exists on the Buying with Us hub or any researched page.
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: That a visual timeline would lift reservation intent; that perceived certainty is the primary emotional driver for choosing new-build.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Emotional-driver and reservation-intent claims are behavioural hypotheses requiring A/B data or CRM validation.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: The FTB page states 'no buying chains' as an advantage but no visual purchase-timeline module exists on the Buying with Us hub. The page currently does X (prose advantage claim without visual demonstration). Public research cannot establish that a visual timeline would lift reservation intent, or that perceived certainty is the primary emotional driver. Hypothesis to validate: a step-by-step timeline may convert the no-chain advantage into perceived certainty. Validate with GA4 engagement data post-launch, CRM reservation-intent feedback and A/B test results.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: 'no buying chains' is claimed on the FTB page; no visual purchase-timeline module exists on the Buying with Us hub. Not established by public research: that a visual timeline would lift reservation intent, or that perceived certainty is the primary emotional driver. Hypothesis to validate: a step-by-step timeline may convert the no-chain advantage into perceived certainty. Validate with: GA4 engagement data, CRM reservation-intent feedback, A/B test results.
material_claims.validation_data_source: GA4 engagement data post-launch, CRM reservation-intent feedback, A/B test results
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: 'Primary emotional driver' was an unproven psychological claim. The replacement labels it as hypothesis and names the exact A/B and CRM data that would validate it.

material_claims.current_R6_wording: suppressing Persimmon's direct-enquiry funnel (enquiry lost to aggregators)
material_claims.directly_observed: No scheme-comparison tool; no alert mechanism on researched pages.
material_claims.inferred_not_proven: The actual volume of direct-enquiry suppression.
material_claims.why_limitation_needed: Suppression volume requires internal traffic and enquiry data.
material_claims.proposed_R6b_wording: No scheme-comparison or alert tool exists on the researched pages. The page currently does X (no re-engagement mechanism). Public research cannot establish the actual volume of direct-enquiry suppression. Validate with GA4, CRM and sales-team data before prioritising against other actions.
material_claims.evidence_limitation_customer_readable: Direct observation: no scheme-comparison or alert tool exists on the researched pages. Not established by public research: the actual volume of direct-enquiry suppression. Validate with: GA4, CRM and sales-team data.
material_claims.why_improves_honesty: Removes the implicit certainty that suppression is occurring at a meaningful scale. The customer decides priority with their own data.
